_layer: IDENTITY (EXAMPLE). Copy this directory to profile/ and replace every value with your own. profile/ is git-ignored and never ships; this example does.
_who: Alex Moreno is fictional. The point of this file is the SHAPE, and especially the fact that a title ceiling, an employment status, and an auto-reject list are things the system needs stated explicitly rather than inferred.

source_documents._career_context_note: PRIMARY source of truth for every metric, date, scope claim, and codename. Read before any fit assessment or build. Put your own career document here - a detailed one beats a polished one.

title_ceiling._rule: State the highest title you actually held. You may APPLY to roles above it; your history is never inflated to match. This is the single most common way a tailored CV starts lying.

employment_status._rule: If you are not currently employed, set this false and give the end month. Some setups ban the word 'Present' in date ranges - see guardrails.json.

auto_reject_employers.Example Corp: Left on bad terms; will not return. Auto-reject any Example Corp role.
auto_reject_employers._note: Company-level exclusions are identity, not policy: they exist because of your history, not because of a search parameter. Delete this block if you have none.

voice._reference: Your own notes on how you write to strangers. Keep it short and specific.
voice.anchor: the credential you most want a hiring manager to remember
voice._rule: ONE honest closing ask. Never imply curiosity you do not have, never hedge with 'if there's good fit', never offer to be deflected to 'the right person'.
